comparator.name: Organization and Management Studies (Organisatie- en Managementwetenschappen)
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026–27 curriculum accounts for exactly 180 ECTS: 60 compulsory ECTS in year 1, 60 compulsory ECTS in year 2, and year 3 with 42 compulsory ECTS plus 18 ECTS of genuine exchange or minor space. Zero-credit GROW development is excluded. The complete 12-ECTS organisational-research project and 12-ECTS thesis remain explicit, and no content is invented for the open choice space.
components: Genuine 18-ECTS open choice space; no elective content is invented.

core: Organisation and management theory, organisational sociology and collaboration within and between organisations
Organisational psychology, human behaviour, leadership and organisational development
Strategy, complex organisational decision-making and management across public and private organisations
Qualitative, quantitative and causal organisational research
Organisational change, advice, intervention and evaluation
adjacent: Innovation, entrepreneurship and responsible organisational change
questions: How do organisations coordinate people, strategy and relationships to function effectively?
How can organisations diagnose, manage and evaluate change?
How can entrepreneurship and innovation support responsible organisational transformation?

candidates.label: Innovation, entrepreneurship and responsible organisational change

selection.assessment: The closest alternative owns organisation theory, sociology, psychology, strategy, collaboration, change, decision-making and public/private management. Innovation and entrepreneurship form one independently coherent direct-interest direction and yield a substantively distinct responsible-change curriculum. All other generator-eligible rows are substantively covered by the closest concept; no third generator-backed direction remains, so production stops at two.

alternatives.label: Organisations, strategy & human behaviour
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum centres organisational sociology and psychology, strategy, collaboration, leadership, change and empirical organisational research.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to Organization and Management Studies: a social-scientific programme on how organisations function, make decisions, coordinate people, communicate, collaborate, innovate and change.
progression: Foundations in organisations, sociology, social psychology, economics, politics, communication and research precede advanced organisational psychology, negotiation, strategic thinking, innovation, leadership, social theory and qualitative inquiry. All formal prerequisites and verified term offerings are respected; seven level-3 courses provide advanced depth.

alternatives.label: Innovation, entrepreneurship & responsible change
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum makes innovation and entrepreneurship the organising direction and connects organisational change to sustainability, ethics, governance and responsible leadership.
alternatives.concept: An organisation-and-management direction built around innovation, entrepreneurship and responsible organisational change, joining business, leadership and research to sustainability, ethics, circular economy and environmental governance.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, seventeen courses shift the centre of gravity from broad organisational sociology, psychology, communication and inter-organisational relations to entrepreneurship, innovation, sustainability, circular economy, ethics and environmental governance. The difference is a substantive programme direction and exceeds the 30-ECTS floor.
progression: Business, research, economics, leadership and sustainability foundations precede advanced organisational psychology, innovation, entrepreneurship, responsible leadership, circular-resource analysis, environmental governance and market research. Sustainability Essentials I precedes II, and all formal prerequisites and verified offerings are respected; nine level-3 courses provide advanced depth.

notes.text: Tilburg prescribes a dense organisation-science sequence spanning organisational sociology and psychology, strategy, methods, networks, development, intervention, a 12-ECTS organisational-research project and a 12-ECTS thesis. UCR can build coherent organisational and responsible-innovation pathways, but it does not reproduce the dedicated labour-law component, the complete methods sequence or the two compulsory research projects; the 18-ECTS free-choice space is preserved as open curriculum.
The Tilburg programme is Dutch-taught, whereas UCR is English-taught. This comparison assesses academic content and structure rather than language of instruction.
